name: Bug report
description: Report a bug in the compiler, runtime, or standard library.
title: "[bug] "
labels: ["bug", "triage"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Thanks for filing a bug. Please include a minimal reproduction —
        a `.kry` program plus the exact command you ran is ideal.
  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: Kryos version
      description: Output of `kryos --version`.
      placeholder: kryos 2.3.0
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: platform
    attributes:
      label: Host OS / arch
      placeholder: Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: dropdown
    id: backend
    attributes:
      label: Backend
      options:
        - cranelift (default — kryos run / kryos build)
        - llvm (kryos build --backend llvm)
        - wasm (kryos build --backend wasm)
        - not sure / multiple
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: repro
    attributes:
      label: Reproduction
      description: A minimal `.kry` snippet and the exact command(s) that trigger the bug.
      render: text
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: expected
    attributes:
      label: Expected behavior
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: actual
    attributes:
      label: Actual behavior
      description: Include any stderr, panic message, or stack trace.
      render: text
    validations:
      required: true

blank_issues_enabled: false
contact_links:
  - name: Q&A and ideas
    url: https://github.com/NORTHTEKDevs/kryos-lang/discussions
    about: Open-ended questions, ideas, and show-and-tell go in Discussions.
  - name: Security report
    url: https://github.com/NORTHTEKDevs/kryos-lang/security/policy
    about: Report a vulnerability privately to info@northtek.io. Do not file a public issue.

name: Feature request
description: Propose a new language feature, stdlib addition, or tooling improvement.
title: "[feature] "
labels: ["enhancement"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Before filing, consider opening a [Discussion](https://github.com/NORTHTEKDevs/kryos-lang/discussions)
        instead if the idea is open-ended. Use this issue template once
        you have a concrete proposal.
  - type: textarea
    id: problem
    attributes:
      label: Problem
      description: What can you not currently do, or what is awkward to do, in Kryos?
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: proposal
    attributes:
      label: Proposal
      description: |
        Concrete syntax and semantics if it's a language feature; API
        sketch if it's a stdlib addition; UX description if it's
        tooling.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: alternatives
    attributes:
      label: Alternatives considered
  - type: textarea
    id: prior-art
    attributes:
      label: Prior art
      description: Equivalent features in Rust, Go, Swift, etc., and how they compare.

<!--
Thanks for contributing to Kryos. A few quick notes:

* Keep PRs focused. One conceptual change per PR is best.
* For language-behavior changes, please include a `.kry` test program in
  `compiler/tests/native/` or wherever the most relevant suite lives.
* Run `cargo test --release -j 2 --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml`
  locally before pushing.
-->

## Summary

<!-- What does this PR do, in one or two sentences? -->

## Motivation

<!-- Why is this change worth making? Link to any related issue or
     discussion. -->

## Implementation notes

<!-- Anything reviewers should know before reading the diff:
     * non-obvious design choices,
     * tradeoffs you considered and rejected,
     * follow-up work intentionally left for a later PR. -->

## Tests

<!-- How did you verify this works? At minimum:
     * which test files cover the new behavior,
     * pass/fail counts before and after, especially the native
       `--release` sweep if you touched codegen/MIR/runtime. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] `cargo build --release` is clean (no warnings).
- [ ] Relevant unit tests pass.
- [ ] Native `--release` sweep still passes (run if you touched
      compiler, MIR, codegen, runtime, or stdlib).
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry added under the next unreleased section, if the
      change is user-visible.

# Starter tasks

This file is a curated list of small, well-scoped tasks for first-time
contributors. They are intentionally narrower than the open issue tracker
and are the right place to land your first PR.

Pick one, comment on the matching issue (or open one referencing this
file), and submit a PR. If no matching issue exists yet, open one with
the `good first issue` label and link the relevant task number below.

---

## Documentation

1. **Add a cookbook recipe.** `docs/learn/cookbook/` currently has six
   recipes. Good candidates for a seventh:
   - **CSV parser:** read a `.csv` file, sum a numeric column, print the
     total. Touches `file_read`, `str_split`, parsing primitives.
   - **TCP echo server:** accept connections in a loop, echo each line
     back. Touches `tcp_listen`, `spawn`, channels.
   - **WebSocket client:** connect to a public echo server, send a
     message, print the reply. Touches `ws_connect` from the stdlib.
   - **SQLite query tool:** open a DB file, run a query passed on the
     command line, print rows. Touches `sqlite_open`, `sqlite_query`.

## Standard library

4. **Add a missing string function.** Audit `compiler/stdlib/string.kry`
   for gaps. Common requests: `str_pad_left`, `str_pad_right`,
   `str_repeat`, `str_count`. Each new function needs:
   - The Kryos implementation in the stdlib module.
   - At least three `@test` cases.
   - A documentation comment matching the existing style.

5. **Add a missing array function.** Same shape as (4), against
   `compiler/stdlib/array.kry`. Candidates: `array_chunk`,
   `array_flatten`, `array_unique`, `array_partition`.

## Examples

7. **Add an example program.** `examples/` showcases concrete
   capabilities. Good additions:
   - **Markdown to HTML converter.** ~150 lines. Show string handling.
   - **JSON-to-CSV converter.** ~100 lines. Show JSON + file I/O.
   - **Mini-templating engine.** Substitute `{{ name }}` style holes in
     a template string from a map.

   Examples must run on `kryos run examples/yourfile.kry` with no
   external setup beyond `examples/`-local files.

## Diagnostics

8. **Improve one error message.** Pick any `kryos-errors`, `kryos-parser`,
   or `kryos-types` diagnostic that you found confusing and:
   - Update its message to say what was expected and what was found.
   - Add a hint line suggesting a fix when there's a clear common cause.
   - Add a snapshot test in the relevant crate.

## Tooling

9. **Add a `kryos new --template <name>` flag.** Today `kryos new <name>`
   scaffolds a default project. Extend it with `--template lib`,
   `--template cli`, `--template http-server` that lay down a starter
   structure for that shape. Each template is a small directory bundled
   with the CLI crate.

10. **Add a `kryos fmt --check` flag.** Today `kryos fmt` rewrites files.
    `--check` should print the diff and exit non-zero without modifying
    anything. Mirrors `rustfmt --check`. Roughly 30–50 lines in
    `kryos-fmt`.

## Editor support

11. **Polish the VS Code extension.** `editors/vscode/`. Open candidates:
    - More snippet completions in `snippets/kryos.json`.
    - Better TextMate grammar handling for `@` decorators.
    - An icon set for the file explorer.

12. **Finish the Zed extension wiring.** `editors/zed/` is a scaffold
    that auto-discovers a `kryos` binary on `PATH`. It needs LSP
    completions to land cleanly; verify with a real Zed install and
    file follow-up issues for any rough edges.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [master, main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master, main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true


jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install native deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Build (release)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Build the full workspace so that kryos-rt and kryos-stdlib-native
        # are produced as staticlibs alongside the kryos binary; the driver
        # looks them up at link time.
        run: cargo build --release -j 2

      - name: Native test runner (JIT + LLVM --release end-to-end)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Runs every fixture through `kryos run` (Cranelift) AND
        # `kryos build --release` (LLVM AOT) with expected-stdout checks.
        # This suite caught parse_float printing 0 on AOT -- a days-old
        # user-facing miscompile that no other CI step covered (the parity
        # corpus lacked the shape). It must run on every platform.
        run: cargo test --release -j 2 -p kryos-test-runner --test native_runner -p kryos-rt

      - name: Smoke test (kryos run tests/smoke.kry)
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ./target/release/kryos run tests/smoke.kry > smoke_output.txt
          printf "30\n2\nKryos\n" > expected.txt
          diff expected.txt smoke_output.txt

      - name: Smoke directory full sweep (tests/smoke/*.kry)
        shell: bash
        # Cranelift JIT path over every smoke test. Reports per-file
        # pass/fail and fails the job on any divergence. Catches
        # regressions the per-file CI step (M1 audit baseline) missed
        # because that step only iterated 1 file.
        run: |
          set -e
          fail=0
          for f in tests/smoke/*.kry; do
            name=$(basename "$f" .kry)
            if ! ./compiler/target/release/kryos run "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "  FAIL  $name"
              fail=$((fail+1))
            else
              echo "  OK    $name"
            fi
          done
          echo "smoke-sweep: $((32 - fail))/32 pass"
          [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

      - name: Example smoke tests
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Run a curated set of examples end-to-end. Each example is required to
        # exit cleanly. This is the cheapest regression gate against
        # codegen / linker / runtime breakage.
        run: |
          set -e
          for ex in hello fibonacci calculator word_count shapes; do
            echo "== examples/$ex.kry =="
            ./target/release/kryos run ../examples/$ex.kry > /dev/null
          done

      - name: Showcase smoke tests
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Showcase apps exercise the wider stdlib surface area: JSON, file I/O,
        # channels, markdown rendering. They must compile and exit cleanly.
        # ssg and kvdb resolve their output paths via env_get(TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP),
        # so the same step works identically on the Windows job.
        run: |
          set -e
          for ex in markdown kvdb ssg worker_pool; do
            echo "== showcase/$ex.kry =="
            ./target/release/kryos run ../examples/showcase/$ex.kry > /dev/null
          done

      - name: Install clang for LLVM AOT
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y clang

      - name: Spec conformance suite (both backends)
        # Self-checking programs organized by reference-manual chapter; the
        # suite found 5 real codegen bugs on its first run (silent match-guard
        # drops, u8 compare sign-extension, narrow-int IR mismatches, bool
        # cast sext, string ordering by pointer).
        run: bash tests/conformance/run_conformance.sh

      - name: Ecosystem + packages typecheck sweep
        # Typechecks all 255 ecosystem/ + packages/ .kry sources from their
        # package roots (a 2026-07-02 sweep found 7 shipped sources that no
        # test executed and that did not typecheck). Negative capability
        # fixtures are excluded by explicit list inside the script.
        run: bash tests/ecosystem_check.sh

      - name: Strict-capabilities gate (examples are exemplary)
        # Every public example/showcase program must pass
        # `kryos check --strict-capabilities` with least-privilege
        # @capabilities declarations. Keeps the language's central pitch
        # (compile-time capability safety) enforced on its own demos.
        run: bash tests/strict_caps_examples.sh

      - name: Inferred-mode soundness gate (deny-by-default cannot leak)
        # Asserts that authority reaches the boundary through every path
        # (direct calls, method/static dispatch, builtin-as-value, and
        # annotated stdlib wrappers) and is REJECTED from an unannotated
        # `main`, while safe/declared code is accepted. Locks in the leaks
        # closed by adversarial review so a refactor cannot silently reopen one.
        run: bash tests/inferred_soundness.sh

      - name: Examples gate (root check + fixtures AOT/JIT + showcase)
        # Type-checks every root example, AOT-compiles + JIT-runs the
        # regression fixtures, and runs the showcase apps. This gate existed
        # but was not wired into CI -- the http_api fixture silently rotted
        # past the deny-by-default flip until a manual run caught it.
        run: bash tests/run_examples_gate.sh

      - name: Examples E2E gate (differential run + served response bodies)
        # The gate above only COMPILES the showcase apps. Three real defects
        # shipped through it: json_bool(false) serving JSON `true` on
        # --release, a struct-returning fn value returning garbage through a
        # router, and tiny_kv self-recursing to a stack overflow on its first
        # command. This one RUNS the apps on both backends, diffs their
        # output, and asserts on real HTTP response bodies.
        run: bash tests/run_examples_e2e.sh

      - name: Security gate (capability attenuation must attenuate)
        # A zero-capability program could read any string in the host process
        # via str_to_ptr + ptr_byte_at and deref arbitrary offsets, while
        # passing --strict-capabilities. Asserts the escape is rejected, that
        # declared ffi still works (no over-rejection), and that the stdlib
        # does not cascade ffi onto ordinary callers.
        run: bash tests/security_gate.sh

      - name: IR signature gate (calls must match their declarations)
        # Guards the bug CLASS behind the json_bool miscompile: a narrow value
        # passed where a wider one is declared leaves the upper bits of the
        # argument register undefined. Found two more latent instances
        # (char_from, string_char_at) that had never surfaced as a failure.
        run: bash tests/ir_signature_gate.sh

      - name: Package selftests (execute every packages/*/src/selftest.kry)
        # ecosystem_check.sh only typechecks packages/; these actually RUN.
        # The dotenv selftest is what exposed the map-value use-after-free.
        run: bash tests/package_selftests.sh

      - name: Encoding robustness (BOM/CRLF accepted, UTF-16 diagnosed)
        # Windows Notepad saves UTF-8 with a BOM; PowerShell `>` writes
        # UTF-16. Sources in real-editor encodings must compile or get an
        # actionable message — a BOM previously produced token soup.
        run: bash tests/encoding_check.sh

      - name: Differential fuzz smoke (JIT vs AOT, 60 random programs)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Generates 60 random type-correct programs and diffs Cranelift-JIT
        # output against LLVM-AOT output. Catches backend miscompiles/
        # divergences (the class the loop-share and value-semantics bugs
        # fell in). Deterministic seed range; the full campaign runs via
        # `python tools/diff-fuzz/gen2.py --count N` locally / on dispatch.
        run: |
          python3 ../tools/diff-fuzz/gen2.py --count 60 --seed-base 777000             --kryos target/release/kryos

      - name: Memory-safety fuzz smoke (KRYOS_FREE_DIAG, 40 programs)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Runs random programs under the runtime's free-diagnostics and
        # fails on any DOUBLE-FREE. Catches heap over-frees that corrupt
        # memory WITHOUT changing observable output -- the class the
        # nested-statement str-temp double-free fell in (which the
        # output-diff smoke above cannot see).
        run: |
          python3 ../tools/diff-fuzz/memsafety_fuzz.py --count 40 --seed-base 888000             --kryos target/release/kryos

      - name: Memory-plateau gate
        # A heavy string+array churn workload must keep peak RSS under a hard

claims.text: Contains 200 lines beginning "# ceiling. The pre-fix build grew to ~10.7GB on this workloa".

span.text:
# ceiling. The pre-fix build grew to ~10.7GB on this workload
        # (2026-07-04); the fixed build plateaus near 4MB. Guards against
        # reintroduced unbounded leaks (Linux GNU time -v).
        run: bash tests/mem_plateau_check.sh

      - name: Backend parity matrix (Cranelift vs LLVM)
        shell: bash
        # Runs every tests/smoke/*.kry under both backends; classifies LLVM
        # failures into A/B/C/D/E/T/A' buckets. Exit 0 only when both
        # backends agree on every test. Lets us track parity regressions
        # over time (results uploaded as artifact).
        run: bash tests/parity/run_parity.sh

      - name: Upload parity report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: parity-linux
          path: tests/parity/results/parity-*.*

  wasm-smoke:
    # WebAssembly backend coverage. Builds every `examples/wasm_*.kry`
    # under `--backend wasm` and executes the result through the Node env
    # host (tools/wasm-host/run.mjs) -- Kryos wasm modules import their
    # runtime from the `env` host module (JS-host contract), they are not
    # WASI modules; wasmtime cannot instantiate them. Catches regressions
    # in the WASM emitter that the native-only smoke battery misses.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install native deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Build (release)
        working-directory: compiler
        run: cargo build --release -j 2

      - name: WASM smoke (every examples/wasm_*.kry)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          KRYOS=./compiler/target/release/kryos
          # wasm_browser_demo + wasm_web_demo target the browser (need DOM
          # bindings + a JS host) and aren't WASI-runnable; skip them.
          fail=0
          built=0
          ran=0
          skipped=0
          for f in examples/wasm_*.kry; do
            name=$(basename "$f" .kry)
            case "$name" in
              wasm_browser_demo|wasm_web_demo)
                echo "  SKIP  $name (browser-target; needs JS host)"
                skipped=$((skipped+1))
                continue
                ;;
            esac
            out=$(mktemp -u).wasm
            if ! "$KRYOS" build "$f" --release --backend wasm -o "$out" 2>&1 > /tmp/build.log; then
              echo "  FAIL  $name (build)"
              cat /tmp/build.log
              fail=$((fail+1))
              continue
            fi
            built=$((built+1))
            if ! node tools/wasm-host/run.mjs "$out" > /tmp/run.log 2>&1; then
              echo "  FAIL  $name (node host run)"
              cat /tmp/run.log
              fail=$((fail+1))
              rm -f "$out"
              continue
            fi
            ran=$((ran+1))
            rm -f "$out"
            # Verify every `// expect-stdout: <text>` line appears in the output
            # (catches SILENT-WRONG regressions, not just build/run failures).
            missing=0
            while IFS= read -r want; do
              if ! grep -qF -- "$want" /tmp/run.log; then
                echo "  FAIL  $name (expected stdout not found: '$want')"
                missing=1
              fi
            done < <(grep -oE '// expect-stdout: .*' "$f" | sed 's|// expect-stdout: ||')
            if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
              echo "    --- actual output ---"; cat /tmp/run.log
              fail=$((fail+1))
              continue
            fi
            echo "  OK    $name"
          done
          echo ""
          echo "wasm-smoke: built=$built ran=$ran skipped=$skipped failed=$fail"
          [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

  selfhost-stage1:
    # Stage 0 → Stage 1 self-host verification (M6).
    # Stage 0: the Rust-based kryos compiler builds.
    # Stage 1: kryos check on every compiler/self-host/*.kry must pass,
    #          plus kryos run compiler/self-host/stage1_mini_parser.kry
    #          must finish with "stage 1 mini-parser: ok" on stdout.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install native deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Build kryos (Stage 0)
        working-directory: compiler
        run: cargo build --release -j 2

      - name: Stage 1 — kryos check every self-host file
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          KRYOS=./compiler/target/release/kryos
          fail=0
          total=0
          for f in compiler/self-host/*.kry; do
            total=$((total+1))
            name=$(basename "$f" .kry)
            if ! "$KRYOS" check "$f" > /tmp/check.log 2>&1; then
              echo "  FAIL  $name"
              cat /tmp/check.log
              fail=$((fail+1))
            else
              echo "  OK    $name"
            fi
          done
          echo ""
          echo "selfhost-stage1 check: $((total - fail))/$total pass"
          [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

      - name: Stage 1 — kryos run stage1_mini_parser.kry
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          KRYOS=./compiler/target/release/kryos
          out=$("$KRYOS" run compiler/self-host/stage1_mini_parser.kry)
          echo "$out" | tail -5
          echo "$out" | grep -q "stage 1 mini-parser: ok" \
            || { echo "expected 'stage 1 mini-parser: ok' marker in stdout"; exit 1; }

  docs-examples:
    # The manual's code blocks are part of the contract: every self-contained
    # ```kryos block in docs/learn/**, the numbered chapters, QUICKSTART.md,
    # and CLAUDE.md must type-check against the current compiler. Three real
    # compiler bugs were found in one day by running examples the docs
    # promised worked (see shift step 222).
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install native deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Build (release)
        working-directory: compiler
        run: cargo build --release -j 2

      - name: Check every docs kryos block
        run: python3 tools/docs-examples/check.py

  registry-smoke:
    # Real HTTP roundtrip against an ephemeral registry server. Proves
    # the protocol path (/v1/health, /v1/packages/<name>, /v1/packages/
    # <name>/<version>, /v1/search) works end-to-end without filesystem
    # shortcuts. Server is spun up on 127.0.0.1:18080 against a
    # synthetic 2-package index in $RUNNER_TEMP.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

- uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "tools/registry"

      - name: Run registry smoke
        run: bash tests/registry/smoke.sh

  quickstart-e2e:
    # End-to-end QUICKSTART.md verification. Walks build → Cranelift JIT
    # → LLVM AOT → WASM/wasmtime → first tour examples in one script.
    # See tests/quickstart_e2e.sh.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install native deps + clang + wasmtime
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config clang
          curl https://wasmtime.dev/install.sh -sSf | bash
          echo "$HOME/.wasmtime/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Run quickstart E2E
        run: bash tests/quickstart_e2e.sh

  fuzz:
    # Smoke-run the three cargo-fuzz targets (lexer, parser, typechecker)
    # for a short fixed time each. Catches regressions where a random byte
    # sequence panics rather than producing a clean error. Long-form
    # fuzzing campaigns run separately (workflow_dispatch); this is the
    # CI-gating step.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          components: rust-src

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler/fuzz"

      - name: Install cargo-fuzz
        run: cargo install cargo-fuzz --locked

      - name: Install native deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Run fuzz_lexer for 60s
        working-directory: compiler
        run: |
          cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_lexer -- -max_total_time=60 -timeout=10

      - name: Run fuzz_parser for 60s
        working-directory: compiler
        run: |
          cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_parser -- -max_total_time=60 -timeout=10

      - name: Run fuzz_typechecker for 60s
        working-directory: compiler
        run: |
          cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_typechecker -- -max_total_time=60 -timeout=10

      - name: Upload fuzz corpus on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: fuzz-corpus
          path: compiler/fuzz/corpus/

  build-and-test-macos:
    # macOS tier-1 verification. Runs on the public-repo macos-14 runner
    # (Apple Silicon, free for public repos). Mirrors the Linux Cranelift
    # smoke battery so M-series regressions get caught at PR time. Intel
    # (macos-13) coverage is added in release.yml's matrix, not here, to
    # keep PR wall time predictable.
    runs-on: macos-14
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install LLVM (Homebrew)
        run: |
          # Provides clang for the LLVM AOT path. Apple's bundled clang
          # also works but Homebrew LLVM matches the Linux job's version.
          brew install llvm
          echo "$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Build (release)
        working-directory: compiler
        run: cargo build --release -j 2

      - name: Native test runner (JIT + LLVM --release end-to-end)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Runs every fixture through `kryos run` (Cranelift) AND
        # `kryos build --release` (LLVM AOT) with expected-stdout checks.
        # This suite caught parse_float printing 0 on AOT -- a days-old
        # user-facing miscompile that no other CI step covered (the parity
        # corpus lacked the shape). It must run on every platform.
        run: cargo test --release -j 2 -p kryos-test-runner --test native_runner -p kryos-rt

      - name: Smoke test (kryos run tests/smoke.kry)
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ./target/release/kryos run tests/smoke.kry > smoke_output.txt
          printf "30\n2\nKryos\n" > expected.txt
          diff expected.txt smoke_output.txt

      - name: Smoke sweep — core language (required)
        shell: bash
        # The stdlib-native surface (net/db/crypto/fs/io/os/process/re/term/
        # async-http) runs in the dedicated required step below; this step
        # covers everything else. Both must pass.
        run: |
          set -e
          DARWIN_PORT="test_async_http_roundtrip test_crypto test_db test_db2 test_fs test_io test_net test_net2 test_os test_process test_re test_term"
          fail=0
          total=0
          for f in tests/smoke/*.kry; do
            name=$(basename "$f" .kry)
            case " $DARWIN_PORT " in *" $name "*) continue;; esac
            total=$((total+1))
            if ! ./compiler/target/release/kryos run "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "  FAIL  $name"
              fail=$((fail+1))
            else
              echo "  OK    $name"
            fi
          done
          echo "smoke-sweep (macos core): $((total - fail))/$total pass"
          [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

      - name: Smoke sweep — stdlib-native (required)
        shell: bash
        # The Darwin native-stdlib port landed (the macOS link now passes
        # -framework Security/CoreFoundation/SystemConfiguration). These
        # net/db/crypto/fs/io/os/process/re/term tests must pass on macOS.
        run: |
          DARWIN_PORT="test_async_http_roundtrip test_crypto test_db test_db2 test_fs test_io test_net test_net2 test_os test_process test_re test_term"
          fail=0
          for name in $DARWIN_PORT; do
            f="tests/smoke/$name.kry"
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            echo "== $name =="
            if out=$(./compiler/target/release/kryos run "$f" 2>&1); then
              echo "  OK    $name"
            else
              # Drop ld 'warning:' noise so the real Undefined-symbols / ld
              # error survives -- that's the diagnostic the port ticket needs.
              grep -vE "ld: warning" <<< "$out" | tail -20
              echo "  FAIL  $name"
              fail=$((fail+1))
            fi
          done
          echo "darwin-port (stdlib-native): $((12 - fail))/12 pass"
          exit $fail

      - name: Example smoke tests
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          for ex in hello fibonacci word_count shapes; do
            echo "== examples/$ex.kry =="
            ./target/release/kryos run ../examples/$ex.kry > /dev/null
          done

      - name: AOT release smoke (hello via LLVM)
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          ./target/release/kryos build --release ../examples/hello.kry -o hello
          ./hello > hello_output.txt
          printf "Hello, Kryos!\n" > hello_expected.txt
          diff hello_expected.txt hello_output.txt

      - name: Backend parity matrix
        shell: bash
        # Re-runs all smoke tests under both backends; the Darwin port
        # landed so this is required on macOS too.
        run: bash tests/parity/run_parity.sh

      - name: Upload parity report
        if: always()

uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: parity-macos
          path: tests/parity/results/parity-*.*

  build-and-test-windows:
    # Windows MSVC tier-1 job. Mirrors the Linux build battery across
    # both backends: Cranelift (`kryos run`) and LLVM AOT (`kryos build
    # --release`). Specifically guards against:
    #   - LNK1107 regressions caused by emitting DWARF metadata into
    #     COFF objects (codegen routes DI through CodeView on Windows
    #     and link.exe consumes it via /DEBUG).
    #   - kryos-codegen-llvm IR-shape regressions (these tests must pass
    #     on Windows too, not just Linux).
    #   - ThinLTO bitcode-into-COFF regressions (LTO is gated off for
    #     Windows/MSVC; kryos-linker has tests that lock the gate in).
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        # The post-job cache save is flaky on Windows runners (tar/zstd over
        # several GiB of target/) and occasionally times out even when the
        # actual build was perfectly green. A failed cache save must NOT
        # mask a successful compile + test cycle.
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Set up MSVC developer environment
        # Exports the same INCLUDE / LIB / PATH that `vcvars64.bat` would,
        # so `link.exe` and `clang` can find msvcrt.lib, ucrt.lib, kernel32.lib,
        # and the Windows SDK without any extra /LIBPATH flags. Our linker
        # crate honors %LIB% when it is set and skips its own discovery.
        uses: ilammy/msvc-dev-cmd@v1
        with:
          arch: x64

      - name: Build (release)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Full workspace release build. Produces kryos.exe, kryos_rt.lib,
        # and kryos_stdlib_native.lib that the driver links at AOT time.
        run: cargo build --release -j 2

      - name: Cargo tests (driver, mir, codegen-llvm, linker)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Tier-1 cargo coverage for the Windows toolchain path:
        #   - kryos-driver: linker invocation + runtime lib lookup
        #   - kryos-mir: platform-agnostic IR
        #   - kryos-codegen-llvm: IR-shape assertions (43 tests, now passing
        #     on both Linux and Windows after the IR-emitter alignment).
        #   - kryos-linker: command-line construction, including the
        #     MSVC /DEBUG flag toggle and the LTO-gated-off-for-MSVC
        #     regression tests.
        run: cargo test --release -j 2 -p kryos-driver -p kryos-mir -p kryos-codegen-llvm -p kryos-linker

      - name: Native test runner (JIT + LLVM --release end-to-end)
        working-directory: compiler
        # Runs every fixture through `kryos run` (Cranelift) AND
        # `kryos build --release` (LLVM AOT) with expected-stdout checks.
        # This suite caught parse_float printing 0 on AOT -- a days-old
        # user-facing miscompile that no other CI step covered (the parity
        # corpus lacked the shape). It must run on every platform.
        run: cargo test --release -j 2 -p kryos-test-runner --test native_runner -p kryos-rt


      - name: Smoke test (kryos run tests/smoke.kry)
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Cranelift path. Should already work on Windows.
        run: |
          ./target/release/kryos.exe run tests/smoke.kry > smoke_output.txt
          printf "30\n2\nKryos\n" > expected.txt
          diff expected.txt smoke_output.txt

      - name: Example smoke tests (Cranelift, kryos run)
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Mirror of the Linux "Example smoke tests" step. Exercises the
        # Cranelift codegen + JIT path on Windows for the same example
        # set Linux runs. calculator is interactive and is intentionally
        # NOT included (it would block on stdin).
        run: |
          set -e
          for ex in hello fibonacci word_count shapes; do
            echo "== examples/$ex.kry (Cranelift) =="
            ./target/release/kryos.exe run ../examples/$ex.kry > /dev/null
          done

      - name: AOT release smoke (kryos build --release examples/hello.kry)
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # The exact regression this job exists to catch. Builds hello.kry
        # via the full LLVM -> clang -> link.exe path and runs the result.
        # Must exit 0 with the expected stdout.
        run: |
          set -e
          ./target/release/kryos.exe build --release ../examples/hello.kry -o hello.exe
          ./hello.exe > hello_output.txt
          printf "Hello, Kryos!\n" > hello_expected.txt
          diff hello_expected.txt hello_output.txt

      - name: AOT release smoke - additional examples
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Broader coverage of the Windows AOT path. Each example exercises
        # different stdlib/codegen surface area: fibonacci (recursion, math),
        # word_count (strings, arrays), shapes (structs, methods).
        # calculator is interactive and is intentionally NOT included.
        run: |
          set -e
          for ex in fibonacci word_count shapes; do
            echo "== examples/$ex.kry (AOT release) =="
            ./target/release/kryos.exe build --release ../examples/$ex.kry -o $ex.exe
            ./$ex.exe > /dev/null
          done

      - name: Showcase smoke tests
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Mirror of the Linux "Showcase smoke tests" step. All four
        # showcase apps are now OS-portable (kvdb and ssg use env_get to
        # resolve a writable temp directory across Unix and Windows).
        run: |
          set -e
          for ex in markdown kvdb ssg worker_pool; do
            echo "== showcase/$ex.kry (Cranelift) =="
            ./target/release/kryos.exe run ../examples/showcase/$ex.kry > /dev/null
          done

      - name: CodeView (.pdb) emission smoke
        working-directory: compiler
        shell: bash
        # Verifies the end-to-end CodeView -> .pdb pipeline:
        #   1. codegen routes DI metadata through the CodeView module flag,
        #   2. clang lowers it via `-gcodeview` into .debug$S/.debug$T
        #      COFF records,
        #   3. link.exe consumes them via /DEBUG and produces a .pdb
        #      sidecar next to the output binary.
        # Without /DEBUG on the linker command line the .pdb is silently
        # dropped; this step catches that regression.
        run: |
          set -e
          ./target/release/kryos.exe build --release -g ../examples/hello.kry -o hello_debug.exe
          if [ ! -f hello_debug.pdb ]; then
            echo "FAIL: hello_debug.pdb was not produced by link.exe /DEBUG"
            ls -la hello_debug*
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: hello_debug.pdb size=$(stat -c%s hello_debug.pdb 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z hello_debug.pdb) bytes"
          ./hello_debug.exe > hello_debug_out.txt
          printf "Hello, Kryos!\n" > hello_debug_expected.txt
          diff hello_debug_expected.txt hello_debug_out.txt

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  # contents:write   — create-release uploads tarballs + attaches release notes
  # id-token:write   — actions/attest-build-provenance requests an OIDC token
  #                    to sign a SLSA-style provenance attestation per artifact
  # attestations:write — store the attestation on the workflow run so users can
  #                      verify with `gh attestation verify`
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write

jobs:
  build-release:
    strategy:
      # One platform's failure must not cancel the other artifacts
      # (the attestation hard-fail wiped the whole v4.43.0 matrix).
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            artifact: kryos-linux-x86_64
          - os: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            artifact: kryos-windows-x86_64
          - os: macos-latest
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            artifact: kryos-macos-x86_64
          - os: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            artifact: kryos-macos-aarch64

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "compiler"

      - name: Install native deps (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Set up MSVC developer environment (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        # Exports INCLUDE / LIB / PATH so link.exe and clang find
        # msvcrt.lib, ucrt.lib, kernel32.lib, and the Windows SDK
        # without extra /LIBPATH flags. The shipped kryos.exe honors
        # %LIB% at runtime but falls back to filesystem discovery on
        # end-user machines without a Developer Prompt active.
        uses: ilammy/msvc-dev-cmd@v1
        with:
          arch: x64

      - name: Build release binary
        working-directory: compiler
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }} -j 4

      - name: Package (Unix)
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist/bin dist/lib dist/stdlib
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos dist/bin/
          # Ship the runtime staticlibs so the installed compiler can link
          # final binaries without re-building the workspace. The compiler
          # looks for these at <bin>/../lib/ at runtime (see kryos-driver::runtime).
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/libkryos_rt.a dist/lib/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/libkryos_stdlib_native.a dist/lib/
          # Also drop them and the binary at the archive root for the
          # install scripts that look for a flat layout.
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos dist/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/libkryos_rt.a dist/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/libkryos_stdlib_native.a dist/
          cp README.md LICENSE CHANGELOG.md dist/
          cp -r examples dist/
          cp -r compiler/stdlib/. dist/stdlib/
          tar czf ${{ matrix.artifact }}.tar.gz -C dist .

      - name: Package (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist/bin dist/lib dist/stdlib
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos.exe dist/bin/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos_rt.lib dist/lib/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos_stdlib_native.lib dist/lib/
          # Flat copies for install scripts that scan the archive root.
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos.exe dist/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos_rt.lib dist/
          cp compiler/target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/kryos_stdlib_native.lib dist/
          cp README.md LICENSE CHANGELOG.md dist/
          cp -r examples dist/
          cp -r compiler/stdlib/. dist/stdlib/
          7z a ${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip ./dist/*

      - name: SHA-256 checksum
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # macOS uses shasum; Linux uses sha256sum; Windows-msys has both.
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              sha256sum ${{ matrix.artifact }}.* > ${{ matrix.artifact }}.sha256
          else
              shasum -a 256 ${{ matrix.artifact }}.* > ${{ matrix.artifact }}.sha256
          fi
          echo "----- ${{ matrix.artifact }}.sha256 -----"
          cat ${{ matrix.artifact }}.sha256

      - name: Attest build provenance (SLSA / OIDC)
        # Lets users run `gh attestation verify <file> --repo NORTHTEKDevs/kryos-lang`
        # to confirm the artifact was built by this exact workflow run.
        # Provides a real chain of custody without paid code-signing certs.
        # GitHub rejects attestations on user-owned PRIVATE repos ("make this
        # repository public to enable") -- that hard-failed the whole matrix
        # and left v4.43.0 with no binaries. Gate on visibility so private
        # builds still ship artifacts; attestation resumes automatically once
        # the repo is public.
        if: ${{ !github.event.repository.private }}
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ matrix.artifact }}.*

      - name: Upload artifact + checksum
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
          path: |
            ${{ matrix.artifact }}.*

  package-vscode:
    # Build the VS Code extension as a .vsix that VS Code can install
    # via "Extensions: Install from VSIX…" and that vsce can publish
    # to the marketplace. The artifact gets attached to the release.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Build + package
        working-directory: editors/vscode
        run: |
          npm install
          npm run compile
          npx --yes @vscode/vsce package -o kryos-vscode.vsix

      - name: Upload .vsix
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: kryos-vscode-vsix
          path: editors/vscode/kryos-vscode.vsix

  package-zed:
    # Build the Zed extension as a wasm32-wasip1 cdylib that Zed loads.
    # Artifact attached to the release alongside the .vsix.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-wasip1

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "editors/zed"

      - name: Build (wasm32-wasip1)
        working-directory: editors/zed
        run: cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1

      - name: Upload .wasm
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: kryos-zed-extension
          path: editors/zed/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/*.wasm

  create-release:
    needs: [build-release, package-vscode, package-zed]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: artifacts

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: artifacts/**/*
          generate_release_notes: true
          draft: false
          # -beta. / -rc. tags publish as prereleases automatically.
          prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-beta.') || contains(github.ref_name, '-rc.') }}

      alloca when the object is a mutable aggregate local; heap/ptr objects keep load+inttoptr.

      builtin recognition. Reverted.)

  step:    183 (session 9 -- 2026-06-01 "Bug B investigation: aggregate-in-i64-slot is an ABI design choice; attempted fix REVERTED")
  date:    2026-06-01
  Attempted the struct-field case of Bug B (unblock json/mcp). Precisely root-caused the whole
  aggregate-struct-field area and found it is a DELIBERATE ABI design, not a localized bug:
    - Struct fields are uniform 8-byte slots; field memory access uses an i64-stride GEP
      (`getelementptr i64, ptr base, i32 field_idx`). To keep that valid, ENUM-typed fields are
      flattened to a bare `i64` in the struct def (e.g. `%ParseResult = type { i64, %Parser }`
      where `.value : JsonValue` is really `{i64,i64,i64}`). COST: `extractvalue` yields i64,
      mismatching the enum aggregate it's used as -> the json/mcp AOT compile errors.
    - ATTEMPTED FIX: make enum fields use their real aggregate type (sig_ty_to_llvm) in both the
      struct decl AND the insertvalue construction. Made the SSA path correct (ef: enum struct
      field -> 8 on both backends) BUT introduced a SILENT MISCOMPILE: a field declared AFTER a
      now->24-byte enum field is mis-addressed by the i64-stride GEP (efm: mutate trailing i64
      field -> AOT 15 vs JIT 17).
    - PROOF it's fundamental: the SAME miscompile ALREADY exists for TUPLE fields on baseline
      (tfm: `struct{v:(i64,i64,i64), n:i64}; r.n=10` -> AOT 6 vs JIT 11) -- tuple fields aren't
      flattened, so the i64-stride GEP is already wrong for them. The enum i64-flattening was
      HIDING this for enums by keeping fields 8 bytes.
    - VERIFIED WORKAROUND: aggregate field LAST is correct (tfl -> 11 both backends) -- no trailing
      field to mis-offset. Documented as CLAUDE.md gotcha #21 (silent AOT miscompile warning).
  DECISION: REVERTED the attempted fix (git checkout codegen.rs) -- shipping a silent miscompile is
  worse than the current clean compile error. Working tree back at 3c048d5. Battery 10/10, examples
  19/23 (the 4 Bug-B cases remain clean COMPILE ERRORS, not miscompiles). Only doc commit this step
  (gotcha #21).
  THE REAL FIX (deliberate, deferred -- needs its own focused effort + design doc): pick ONE --
    (A) box/unbox aggregates in i64 field slots: keep 8-byte i64 fields, box an aggregate field to
        a heap ptr on store, unbox (load) on read. Adds heap alloc + ownership per aggregate field;
        also covers the spawn i64-env case (with cross-thread ownership). OR
    (B) migrate ALL struct field memory access from i64-stride GEP to struct-type-indexed GEP
        (`getelementptr %Struct, ptr, i32 0, i32 field_idx`) + typed per-field load/store, and let
        fields hold real aggregate types. Abandons the uniform-8-byte model; also fixes the
        pre-existing tuple-field-mutation miscompile (tfm).

    more localized but adds boxing/ownership. Either is a design-level change -- do NOT attempt
    piecemeal (this step proved piecemeal trades one bug for a worse one).

## Headline

**All 7 benchmarks are within 1.42x of Rust, and Kryos beats Rust and/or

and these numbers were re-measured on rc.2 AFTER the memory-model overhaul
(HeaderPool, share-retain let-bindings, independent-copy array rebinds):

no WSL distro), and we do not fabricate numbers. Reference ports + harness
support are in [`benchmarks/mojo/`](./benchmarks/mojo/) - `measure.py` builds
and times them automatically when a `mojo` binary is on PATH. Published
positioning: Mojo lowers MLIR -> LLVM (same backend as clang/rustc), so on tight
numeric kernels (mandelbrot/nbody/matmul/fib) optimized Mojo lands in the same
~1.0-1.7x-of-Rust band these benchmarks already occupy; one cited numeric
benchmark put Mojo ~1.6x of Rust. There is no broad, independent public
shootout, and allocation/pointer-chasing (binary_trees-style) is undocumented
for Mojo. Net: Kryos's numeric-kernel results are in Mojo's league; a true

### binary_trees: from 6.1x to 1.45x (leak-free)

The original port stored each child as a single-element `[Tree]` array =
**three** heap allocations per child (array header + data buffer + boxed
struct). It is now `Tree { left: Option<Shared<Tree>>, right: Option<Shared<Tree>> }`
= **one** arc allocation per node (the new, completed `Shared<T>` heap pointer).
Recursive refcounted teardown is wired (each node's arc block carries a
`__kryos_arc_drop_<T>` drop function, so releasing a tree's root cascades), so
the run is **leak-free: 24 MB peak** (was 1.1 GB while the teardown was missing)
- an apples-to-apples comparison against the freeing C/Rust/Go ports. The
residual 1.45x vs Rust is mostly Rc refcount traffic vs Rust's `Box`
unique-ownership; Go (0.488s) wins via its GC bump allocator. checksum 14723759,

## Methodology

1. **Workloads sized** so the fastest competitor needs >= ~0.3s (fib(40),
   1000x1000x1000-iter mandelbrot, 2M-step nbody, 512x512 matmul, depth-16
   binary_trees, 1M-entry hashmap).
2. **Median of 5 runs** after a warmup; min..max spread in `results.json`.
3. **Startup floor measured separately** (not subtracted, so numbers are honest
   wall-clock): kryos native exe ~5.2ms, rust ~5.7ms, python ~40ms.
4. **Same answer required** - every port prints an identical checksum,
   cross-checked before timings count (fannkuch `73196 / Pfannkuchen(10) = 38`,
   binary_trees 14723759, hashmap 999999000000).
5. **Broken/absent ports are labeled n/a, not buried, and never fabricated.**

## What changed (2026-07-10, rc.2 re-measure)

Full re-run on the rc.2 binary after the memory-model overhaul (type-stable
`HeaderPool` header recycling, retain-on-read borrow fixes), the
value-semantics fixes (share-retain container let-bindings, independent-copy
array rebinds via `kryos_array_dup`), and the ~8,000-program differential
fuzz campaign. Every number is within run-to-run noise of the June sweep —
**the correctness work did not cost performance**: nbody 1.34x -> 1.31x,
binary_trees 1.45x -> 1.42x, matmul still beats Rust (0.96x), hashmap still
beats everything (0.65x of Rust). Same checksum cross-validation; all rows
output-identical across languages before timing.

## What changed (2026-06-14)

Cumulative this session, all gated on backend parity (58 smoke tests, both
backends, 0 divergences) + conformance 6/6 + examples 80/80 + the self-host
bootstrap (stage-2 == stage-3 == stage-4, fixed point held):

- **Reverted an unsound in-place string-concat fast path** (it corrupted every
  aliased `str` reference - interpolation / `let y=a+b` / fn args / container
  stores - and self-concat; the compiler's refcount does not track aliases).
- **TBAA on array element-vs-header accesses** -> fannkuch 1.10x -> 1.01x.
- **Map probe uses `& (cap-1)`** (power-of-two capacity) + added the hashmap
  benchmark (beats Rust and C++).

## Still planned

- nbody's residual 1.34x: fair loop unroll/vectorize hints (the trip count is a
  runtime `let n = 5`, blocking full unroll).
- binary_trees's residual 1.45x: a unique-ownership `Box` (no refcount) or an
  arena would close most of the gap to Rust, but Rc-like `Shared` is the
  idiomatic, safe default and is already competitive.
- A liveness-gated consuming string-append intrinsic (the sound version of the
  reverted fast path).
- The Cranelift column exists for honesty about `kryos run` (the dev backend);
  ship release binaries with `kryos build --release`.

## Startup floors (median of 5)

| Runtime | Floor |
|---|---|
| kryos native exe | 6.0ms |
| rust native exe | 5.5ms |
| python interpreter | 364.7ms |

The python floor measured 40ms in the June sweep and 365ms here — cold-start
interpreter launch on Windows is dominated by environment effects (antivirus
scanning, filesystem cache state), so treat the python floor as indicative
only. The kryos and rust floors are stable across sweeps (5-6ms).

### Fixed — both concurrency release blockers, one root cause (Pass 47)

- **Spawn wrappers passed aggregate captures with the wrong ABI.**
  `conf_spinlock_mutex` and `conf_errors_concurrency` both deadlocked under
  LLVM AOT while passing under Cranelift, and were tracked as two separate
  bugs. They were one. A `__spawn_`/`__coopspawn_` wrapper's aggregate param
  was emitted as `ptr byval(T)` — the by-value-in-memory ABI, which consumes
  no integer register on x86-64 SysV — while the runtime passes one
  pointer-sized word per captured env slot. The wrapper read its enum off the
  stack and took the next declared param from the first integer register, i.e.
  env slot 0 (the boxed enum pointer), so a `send` used that pointer as its
  channel handle and the matching `recv` blocked forever. Spawn wrappers now

claims.text: Documents "Fixed — two aggregate/ownership miscompiles, one per backend (Pass 46)".

span.text:
### Fixed — two aggregate/ownership miscompiles, one per backend (Pass 46)

- **LLVM/AOT: an aggregate-returning function called through a fn VALUE
  returned garbage.** `let f = mk  let w = f()`, where `mk() -> Response`
  returns a struct, read `w.body` as a raw pointer reinterpreted as data (a
  string length in the trillions) or overran the stack on `build --release`,
  while a direct `mk()` and `kryos run` were both correct. `emit_function`
  lowers every aggregate return through the sret out-param ABI, but
  `func_ret_types` records the LOGICAL return type, so the closure env-thunk
  emitted `call %Response @mk()` — no sret argument — against a callee that
  writes through its first parameter. The thunk now reads the callee's real
  aggregate return from `func_sig_aggs`, allocates the box it has to return

### Fixed — duplicate-name soundness sweep (Pass 45)
Eleven shapes of duplicate names that the checker silently accepted (which
duplicate "won" was implementation-defined, or the program died later as an
internal codegen dump) are now clean check-time errors, each with a
type-soundness regression:

- **Struct fields** — duplicate field in a declaration (`struct P { x, y, x }`)
  and in a literal (`P { x: 1.0, x: 2.0 }`).
- **Enum variants** — `enum E { A(i64), B, A(str) }` (variants are tag-indexed
  by position, so dispatch was ambiguous).
- **Parameters** — duplicate names in function, method, and closure parameter
  lists (`fn f(a: i64, a: i64)`, `|x, x| x` — the last duplicate silently won).

span.text:
### Fixed — adversarial cert Passes 35-39 (~30 correctness + crash bugs)
A sustained multi-agent adversarial sweep (JIT-only finders + independent
both-backend re-verification) across pattern matching, closures, concurrency,
generics, numerics, the pipe operator, and drop-path ownership. Every fix ships
with a conformance/type-soundness regression; conformance stayed 15/15 and the
self-host bootstrap 16/16 throughout.

- **Pattern matching.** Bare payload-less enum variants in tuple patterns
  (`(Red, Red)` vs `(Green, Green)`), nested-in-payload (`Pair((Red, k))`),
  direct-payload (`Has(Red)`), and depth-3+ nested leaves (`L3a(L2a(L1a))`) now
  DISCRIMINATE — previously they were parsed as bindings so the first arm always
  won (silent-wrong both backends). Enum-with-nested-payload as a tuple element

### Fixed — concurrency + performance (cert Pass 40)
- **`std::sync` mutex deadlock under real cross-thread contention.** The
  primitive backing `AtomicInt`/`AtomicBool`/`WaitGroup` stored a `MutexGuard`
  behind a shared mutable pointer and released the lock *before* nulling it —
  a waking thread's guard got clobbered, its later unlock failed, and the lock
  leaked held: a program-wide deadlock (4 threads × 500 `fetch_add` hung on
  both backends). Replaced with a race-free atomic spin-then-yield lock.
- **Method-chain compile time was O(2^depth), now linear.** `infer_expr_type`
  on a method call inferred the receiver twice per level (once directly, once
  via `infer_type_name`), so a 30-deep `b.inc().inc()…` chain took >90s. A
  100-deep chain now compiles in ~0.5s.

claims.text: Documents "Fixed — thread-safe ARC, struct-copy ownership, WaitGroup (cert Pass 44)".

span.text:
### Fixed — thread-safe ARC, struct-copy ownership, WaitGroup (cert Pass 44)
- **Refcounts are now atomic** (array/map/string headers): concurrent
  cross-thread releases previously corrupted counts into premature frees —
  50-thread stress segfaulted on 100% of runs; now passes repeatedly on both
  backends with no measurable single-thread perf cost.
- **`let copy = struct` is memory-safe and spec-conformant.** The old move
  lowering re-"moved" the same value every loop iteration (single-threaded
  heap corruption in ~200 iterations); cleanly-clonable structs now deep-copy
  heap fields per the documented ownership model.
- **Spawn blocks own their struct captures** (deep-copied into the spawn env
  on both backends) — the canonical per-iteration WaitGroup capture idiom no
  longer frees the capture before the thread runs.

### Fixed — `kryos test` works on real test files (cert Pass 43)
- **Selective imports no longer falsely collide.** `use std::string::{split_lines}`
  plus `use std::re` failed with "duplicate function `split` imported from
  multiple modules" — the collision was between std::re's *exported* `split`
  and a std::string *internal helper* the user never imported. Non-selected
  transitive helpers now get module-private names.
- **`kryos test` no longer crashes on stdlib-importing or `@capabilities`
  tests.** The test runner's in-process JIT was missing dozens of native
  symbols the AOT path resolves at link time ("can't resolve symbol
  str_to_ptr" / "kryos_db_open" process aborts). The symbol inventory is now
  generated from the sources at build time, ending the drift class.
- Known limitation (documented): a runtime *panic* (not a failed assert)
## [1.0.0-rc.2] — 2026-07-10 — "Memory-sound and launch-hardened"

### Fixed — memory model (the headline)
- **Self-host bootstrap heap corruption healed.** Freeing container headers
  (rc.1) turned historically-forgiven stale releases into ntdll heap
  corruption at merged-compile scale. Root causes fixed: borrow/own
  confusion at container reads (map-get / element / field reads and str
  params now retain via `*_retain_opt`), plus TYPE-STABLE header recycling
  (`HeaderPool`) so residual stale releases are harmless with flat RSS
  (400-round churn soak: 1.1 GB peak vs 10.3 GB pre-fix). The byte-identical
  fixed point (stage-2 == stage-3 == stage-4) reproduces deterministically.
- **@copy struct drop semantics unified across backends** — Cranelift now
  skips @copy struct drops like LLVM (share + no-op drop); the merged
  self-host compile reports ZERO double-frees under `KRYOS_FREE_DIAG`.

### Fixed — correctness
- **LLVM AOT called f64-bits-returning runtime fns as `call double`**:
  `println(to_string(parse_float("3.14")))` printed `0` on release builds
  (reads XMM0, callee sets RAX). Affected parse_float / float() / tensor
  reads. New parity test locks the shape.
- **Narrow-int struct fields (i8/i16/i32) miscompiled on LLVM** (no sext
  into i64 slots; clang rejected the module). Also unlocked
  `kryos build --release` on the 21k-line self-host source.
- **std::csv: a stray mid-field quote silently swallowed the rest of the
  document** — RFC 4180 quote-at-field-start gating; stray quotes are data.
- **stdlib/iter.kry `zip()` and `take()` were broken for all callers**
  (reassigned immutable locals) — caught by the new import validation.

### Added — developer experience
- **Selective imports validated at the use site** with did-you-mean
  (`module X has no export Y`); enum variants and extern items count.
- **`kryos fmt` formats commented files** (line-anchored comment
  re-insertion; refuses — skips, never destroys — when unsure). Previously
  every commented file was skipped.
- **`kryos check` surfaces lexer diagnostics** (unterminated string now
  points at the opening quote instead of a parser cascade).
- **`kryos build --release .` names the binary after the package**
  (`myapp.exe`, not `out.exe`).
- **Free-site forensics** for runtime debugging: `KRYOS_FREE_DIAG=1`
  (+`_MAX`, `_STACK`), `KRYOS_MIR_DROP_TAGS`, `KRYOS_EMIT_FREE_TAGS`.

### CI
- The native test runner (155 fixtures through BOTH backends with output
  checks) now runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows — the coverage hole that
  hid the parse_float miscompile.
- Parity corpus 68 tests, stdout-diffed JIT vs AOT on all three platforms.

### Added — first-run experience
- **`kryos run` project mode.** Bare `kryos run` (and `kryos run <dir>`) now
  resolves the project's `src/main.kry`, mirroring `kryos check`/`kryos build`
  and cargo's bare `run` — previously the documented `kryos new` -> `kryos run`
  flow failed with "required arguments not provided". Program args follow the
  path (`kryos run . World`). A malformed `kryos.toml` is now reported (it was
  silently ignored on the file path).
- **Newcomer-mistake diagnostics.** Targeted errors/hints for the habits every
  Rust/JS/Python developer brings on day one:
  - `println!("hi")` -> "Kryos has no macros — call `println(...)` without the
    `!`" (previously parsed as boolean `not` and surfaced as a baffling bool
    type-mismatch);

### Removed
- **The undocumented global `null` binding** (an i64 = 0 "FFI sentinel" that
  nothing in the stdlib, examples, or ecosystem actually used). `let x = null`
  silently compiled to integer 0 — it is now an error with the Option hint
  above, matching the documented "no null" semantics.

### Security
- Bumped transitive `cmov` 0.5.3 -> 0.5.4 (RUSTSEC advisory: wrong results on
  aarch64 with high register bits set).

## [1.0.0-rc.1] — 2026-07-06 — "Release candidate"

First 1.0 release candidate. This is the "last call" before the SemVer 1.0
stability lock: the language, CLI, MIR/runtime ABI, and registry format are
proposed frozen. Report anything before 1.0.0 final.

- 157 feature probes across three completeness-audit tiers, 0 defects on both

- All release gates green: native corpus (131x2), 495 unit tests, capability

## [1.0.0-beta.5] — 2026-07-06 — "Non-blocking async I/O"

### Added
- **Non-blocking async I/O.** A blocking I/O op (`sleep`, `http_get`,
  `tcp_connect`/`accept`/`send`/`recv`) inside an `async` task now yields the
  cooperative scheduler for the duration of the syscall, so `coop_spawn`ed tasks
  run concurrently — their I/O overlaps instead of serializing. Four async tasks
  each doing 300 ms of I/O finish in ~300 ms, not 1.2 s (verified concurrent on
  both backends). Implemented as a thread-per-task scheduler that releases the
  baton on blocking calls (`kryos_coop_io_begin`/`io_end`/`io_offload`;
  `coop_run` waits for away tasks), not an epoll/IOCP reactor — the observable
  behavior is concurrent async I/O. `examples/async_io.kry` + a threshold-based
  native regression test. The deterministic `await` interleave semantics are
  unchanged.
## [1.0.0-beta.4] — 2026-07-06 — "Actors work; nothing checked permissively"

### Added
- **Actors are fully implemented** on both backends (JIT + AOT). `ActorName()`
  spawns an actor on its own OS thread; `handle.method(args)` sends a message;
  the actor processes messages one at a time, in order, mutating private state
  via `self.field`. Message arguments (i64, str, arrays) are transmitted through
  the mailbox. At `main` exit the runtime drains every mailbox and joins the
  threads, so all messages sent before `main` returns are processed with no
  `sleep` needed. `examples/actors.kry` + a native regression test. (Actors were
  a broken preview in beta.3; the fix corrected the dispatch arg count, handler
  lowering, actor-handle type erasure, an LLVM SSA/pointer-arg bug, and added a
  graceful join.)
- **`time_millis()`** builtin — the documented short alias for

### Changed
- **The entire ecosystem is now deny-by-default.** Every ecosystem package entry
  point declares its capabilities; the ecosystem gate runs under `inferred`
  (253/253 clean). Combined with the compiler default, examples, and self-host
  compiler, **no first-class Kryos code is checked permissively** — only
  internal test-harness fixtures and illustrative doc snippets.
- Concurrency documented accurately: concurrent I/O works today via
  `spawn`/channels/`actor` (real OS threads); `async`/`await` is a cooperative
  CPU-task interleaver, not a non-blocking I/O reactor. Removed the misleading
  "concurrent I/O is unavailable" framing.
- `std::iter` HOFs (`fold`/`filter`/`map`/`reduce`) documented as needing an
  import (they are not global builtins).

## [1.0.0-beta.3] — 2026-07-05 — "Deny-by-default"

The capability model — Kryos's defining feature — is now enforced **by
default**. A loose `kryos run foo.kry` with no flag and no project file rejects
any undeclared authority (filesystem, network, process, environment, crypto,
db, terminal) at compile time. You declare a program's authority once on `main`;
the compiler infers every interior helper and proves nothing exceeds the
declared boundary.

### Added
- **Interior capability inference (`inferred` mode).** A third enforcement mode
  between `permissive` and `strict`: deny-by-default *at the boundary* with
  interior inference. `main` (and any annotated function) must hold every
  capability its code transitively uses; helpers need no annotation — their
  capability set is inferred as a fixpoint over the call graph. Ergonomic *and*
  safe: the ~15k-line self-host compiler is deny-by-default clean with a single
  `@capabilities(fs:read, fs:write, process)` on `main`.
- **`--capabilities-mode=<permissive|inferred|strict>`** on `kryos check` and
  `kryos build`; **`[capabilities] mode`** in `kryos.toml`. `kryos new` scaffolds
  `mode = "inferred"`.
- CI soundness gate (`tests/inferred_soundness.sh`, 16 probes) locking every

### Changed
- **The global default is now `inferred`** (was `permissive`). Deny-by-default
  for every `kryos run` / `check` / `build`. Opt out with
  `--capabilities-mode=permissive` or `[capabilities] mode = "permissive"`.
- Standard-library authority wrappers are annotated so their capabilities
  propagate to callers (`std::fs`, `std::process` env, `std::os`, `std::io`
  file ops, `std::db`); `std::term` corrected from `io` to `term`.
- `env_get` / `env_set` require `process` (reading the environment can
  exfiltrate secrets), documented explicitly.

span.text:
### Fixed (capability soundness — three adversarial review rounds)
- Authority through **method / static dispatch** (`obj.write()`, `Type::m()`)
  was never enforced — a hole present since the checker existed (strict mode
  too). Now gated via call-site propagation.
- Gated builtins used as **first-class values** — passed as `fn` arguments,
  bound with `let`, returned, or stored in arrays/structs — no longer smuggle
  authority past the boundary.
- Stdlib wrappers reaching authority via raw `kryos_*` externs (`env_get_or`,
  `env_has`, `create_dir_all`, the `os` platform helpers, `io::File`, `db`
  cursors) no longer leak — they are annotated.
- **`sleep(ms)`** slept ~0ms: the i64 millisecond argument was reinterpreted as
  f64-seconds bits. Now routes to `kryos_sleep_ms`.

### Preview / honest boundaries
- **Actors remain preview and are rejected at compile time on purpose.** An
  implementation attempt this release confirmed the actor *runtime* is
  incomplete — message arguments are not transmitted and handlers do not
  execute reliably — so a callable constructor would compile to a spawn that
  silently does nothing. Use `spawn` + channels for message-passing. See
  docs/09-concurrency.md.

  `coop_run` / `await`) genuinely interleaves tasks on both backends
  (`A0 B0 A1 B1 A2 B2`), correcting stale "grammar only / synchronous" claims.

### Changed
- Claims audit: README + docs corrected to measured reality (stdlib module

- Actors reframed as preview (parsing + lowering present; constructor not

## [4.46.0] — 2026-06-10 — "@budget: compiler-enforced AI spending ceilings"

### Added
- **`@budget(tokens = N, calls = M)` function attribute** — the wedge feature.
  Entering the function pushes a thread-local budget frame; every `std::llm`
  call inside it (at any depth) pre-charges one model call and post-charges
  actual token usage. Exceeding a ceiling throws `llm error: @budget ...`,
  halting runaway agent loops no matter what their conditions say. Frames pop
  on every return and self-heal across exception unwinds; nested budgets
  stack (an outer frame constrains everything inside). Omitted axes are
  unlimited. Implemented as MIR injection — identical on both backends.
- **E0111 now covers call arguments** — `f(999)` into `fn f(x: u8)` is a
  compile error, completing the literal range-check story (let, const,
  assignment, and now arguments).

### Fixed
- **Selective imports carry method dependencies.** `use m::{SomeStruct}`
  imported the struct's impl methods but not the module-local helpers they
  call — consumers got "undefined variable" from inside library methods
  unless they imported the helpers themselves. The transitive-closure pass
  now walks impl/actor/const bodies too.
